pages.title: Prophet Noah (pbuh)
pages.content:
Prophet Noah (pbuh) is one of the five Prophets of Great Determination (ulu’l azm in Arabic) in Islam. He is known for his great determination and strong belief in Allah. The 71st chapter of the Qur’an bears his name and describes his struggle for Tawhid (Oneness of Allah). His people were drowned in the Great Flood by Allah’s judgment because they did not believe in his message. This event is known as Noah’s Flood.

According to Islamic sources, early generations from Adam (pbuh) lived with the belief in one Allah until the era of Prophet Noah (pbuh). Idolatry first appeared among Noah’s people. For this reason, Allah sent Noah (pbuh) to turn his people away from idols and guide them back to the belief in the Oneness of Allah.

In Islamic sources, Noah (pbuh) was the prophet who lived the longest. The Qur’an gives this information about his age: “We sent Noah to his people, and he stayed with them for 950 years (a thousand years minus fifty years). Then, the flood took the wrongdoers away. But Allah saved Noah (pbuh) and the people on the Ark, making it a sign for everyone.” (Surah Ankabut, verses 14–15) These verses show that Noah (pbuh) stayed with his people for 950 years. However, it is not clear if this period was his whole life, his time as a prophet, or just the time before the flood. According to Islamic reports, Noah was the first prophet after Idris (pbuh) and he worked as a carpenter.

pages.title: The Flood in Ancient Stories
pages.content:
The oldest flood stories come from ancient Middle Eastern tablets which were written in Sumer and Babylon.

The most complete description of the flood story from the Babylonians is found in the Epic of Gilgamesh. In this Babylonian version, the story is told as follows: after the death of his friend, Gilgamesh, King of Uruk, is deeply sad and wants to bring his friend back to life. So, he goes on a journey to find Uta-napishtim, who survived the Flood and became immortal. The King hopes to learn the secret of eternal life. According to the epic, Uta-napishtim learns the gods will send a great flood to destroy humankind because of their noise, but the god Ea warns Uta-napishtim to build a ship to survive. The flood lasts six days and seven nights, and the ship lands safely on a mountain. As a result, those on board are saved.

pages.title: What the Qur’an Says About His People
pages.content: According to the Qur’an, as mentioned in Surah Nûh verses 1–4, Noah (pbuh) warned his community not to worship anyone except Allah and told them about a painful punishment if they refused to listen. According to Surah adh-Dhariyat verse 46 and Surah an-Najm verse 52, his people were very cruel, rebellious, and morally lost. Instead of thinking deeply about Noah’s message, they called him crazy, accused him of lying, and threatened to stone him to death (Surah ash-Shu‘ara verse 116; Surah al-Qamar verse 9). Finally, they challenged Noah and asked him to bring the punishment that he warned them about right away. (Surah Hûd verse 32)

pages.title: The Idols of Noah’s People
pages.content:
As narrated by Ibn Abbas, who was one of the companions of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and an important scholar of tafsir and fiqh, the Prophet (pbuh) said: “The period between Adam and Noah was ten centuries.” (Ibn Sa‘d, al-Tabaqat al-Kubra, Beirut, I, 42)

According to the Qur’an, Noah’s people worshipped statues instead of Allah. Surah Nûh verse 23 says Noah’s people worshipped five particular idols: Wad, Suwa’, Yaghus, Ya’uk, and Nasr. Although Prophet Noah (pbuh) invited them to worship Allah alone, they believed these idols could give them wealth and protect them from danger, and they still insisted on their false belief.

Originally, these were the names of good and righteous men in the past. After they died, people made statues of them to remember their good actions. However, later generations forgot the real story of the statues and eventually, they began worshipping them directly. This is how idol worship developed.

pages.title: Noah Calls His People
pages.content:
Allah sent Noah (pbuh) to guide his people with His message. He was a very patient man and a great speaker who always talked about Allah’s power and authority over the creation. He explained again and again that the perfect balance between day and night, the sun, and the moon shows Allah’s great, infinite power and control. Because Allah owns everything in the heavens and the earth, there can only be one true Creator. Therefore, Noah (pbuh) told his people that worshipping handmade idols of stone, wood, or metal is illogical. He tried to demonstrate that blind faith in these statues limits human potential and stops free thinking. In a sense, it means the enslavement of human beings.

Noah (pbuh) never gave up inviting his people to Allah’s message and reminded them of His severe judgment. According to the Qur’an, whenever he called his people to the truth, they covered their heads with their clothes and put their fingers in their ears, so they would not hear him. (see Surah Nûh, verse 7) For centuries, his people treated him with great cruelty, beat him, and mocked him. However, Noah (pbuh) continued his mission.

Prophet Noah’s message of hope, equality, and justice brought peace to the poor and they paid attention to his message and believed it. Yet, the rich and powerful leaders rejected it. As they wanted to keep their wealth and control, the elites argued with Noah (pbuh). They refused to believe he was a true Messenger. They said, “You are just an ordinary man like us” (Surah Hûd verse 27).

While Noah’s message began to spread among society’s poor and helpless groups and the laborers, the elites felt threatened. The rich leaders told Noah (pbuh) they would only believe in Allah if he left his poor and humble followers. They said that rich and poor people could not share the same belief. Noah (pbuh) completely refused to send his modest and faithful friends away. He pointed out that these people sincerely believed in Allah, so he had no right to reject them. Instead, he asked the leaders to use their common sense and accept the truth.

The conflict continued, and the debates between Noah (pbuh) and the disbelievers became more serious. When the disbelievers lost all their arguments and had nothing left to say, they started to act rudely and look down on Allah’s prophet. “The leaders of his people said, ‘Verily, we see you in plain error.’” (Surah A‘râf, verse 60)

Prophet Noah (pbuh) invited them to worship Allah alone and abandon their false gods for a very long time, for exactly 950 years. However, every new generation was warned by their parents not to believe Noah (pbuh) and to stand against him.

Then, Allah told Prophet Noah (pbuh) that no more people would believe in his message (see Surah Hûd verse 36). The Creator advised him not to be sad about the disbelievers anymore. When Noah’s suffering became too heavy to bear, he stopped hoping for them. Finally, he prayed to Allah and asked Allah not to leave any unbelievers on earth because he believed they would misguide people and would only produce sinful children. (see Surah Nûh, verses 26–27)

Allah accepted Noah’s prayer. The decision was made, and Allah was going to punish the disbelievers with a great flood. Allah commanded Noah (pbuh) to follow His knowledge and instructions and build an ark.

pages.title: Noah Builds the Ark
pages.content:
Noah (pbuh) chose a quiet place very far from the sea. He collected wood and tools, and he worked hard day and night to build the ark. When the leaders of his people passed by, they laughed at him. They said, “Noah, did you stop being a prophet to become a carpenter? Why are you building a huge ship in the middle of nowhere without any water? How will it float? Will you pull it yourself, or do you expect the wind to move it by magic?”

Noah (pbuh) replied: “Soon you will see who will face humiliation and suffering.”

When Noah (pbuh) finished building the ark, he started waiting for Allah’s command. Allah told him that the Flood would start, and that it was time to move, when water began to overflow from the earth.

The terrible day arrived when water miraculously gushed out, which was the divine sign that the great flood was beginning. Noah (pbuh) hurried to the ship he had built and called the few people who believed in Allah to come on board. Following Allah’s command, he also brought a male and a female from every kind of living creature, including animals and birds. As the disbelievers watched him gather the animals, they laughed loudly and mocked him. They thought Noah (pbuh) had lost his mind and wondered what he would do with all those creatures.

pages.title: The Number of Believers
pages.content:
Noah’s wife and his son did not believe his message. They refused to get on the Ark with him. His wife openly showed that she did not believe. His son did not accept the faith either. He chose to stay away from the believers. Just like them, the majority of the people rejected Noah’s words and decided not to enter the ship.

Islamic scholars have different ideas about how many people were on the Ark with Noah (pbuh). Ibn Abbas said there were 80 believers. But some people said the number was 72. Meanwhile, others say there were only 10 people with him.

vocabulary.definition: Refused to accept or believe something.
People who have studied a subject for a long time.

hotspots.title: His Family
hotspots.description: Noah’s wife and his son did not believe his message.

languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read the sentence. Then choose the answer.
languageFocusExercises.question: “His son did not accept the faith either.” What does “either” mean here?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: We use “either” at the end of a negative sentence to mean “also”. In a positive sentence, we use “too”.

Some people said the number was 72. Meanwhile, [choice] say there were only 10 people with him.
His son did not accept the faith [choice].

pages.title: The Flood
pages.content:
Heavy rain poured from the sky as water burst from every crack in the ground. The water level rose continuously. Then, suddenly a strong movement from deep inside pushed the bottom of the ocean up. Soon, sea waves covered the dry land.

In that moment of horror, Noah (pbuh) asked the believers to board the ship, saying that it would sail and stop in the name of Allah. The ship moved through huge waves, and Noah (pbuh) called his son to join them and stay away from the disbelievers. The son refused. He believed a mountain would save him. But a wave separated them and he drowned, as nothing can stop Allah’s judgment.

Then, Allah ordered the earth to absorb its water and the sky to stop raining. The water went away, and the Flood ended. Prophet Noah’s ark safely landed on Mount Judi. Finally, Allah declared: “Away with the wrongdoing people.” (Surah Hûd, verse 44) This great flood removed the people who believed in other gods besides Allah and disobeyed Him.

vocabulary.definition: Came down fast and in large amounts from.
Came out suddenly and strongly from.
Came down and stopped on.
Died under water.

pages.title: The Believers Come Ashore
pages.content:
Noah (pbuh) released the birds and animals to spread across the earth. Right after that, the believers stepped off the ark without any harm. Noah (pbuh) immediately bowed with his forehead to the ground to pray and show his gratitude. The survivors then gathered around a newly made fire. During the flood, making a fire on the wooden ship was not allowed. Nobody could have a warm, cooked meal during the whole journey. So, it was a huge relief for everyone.

According to a report, Prophet Noah (pbuh) and his followers left the Ark on the tenth day of Muharram, called Ashura. They fasted on this day to thank Allah for saving them from the big flood. This fasting tradition was very old. Even before Islam, people in Mecca fasted on Ashura because it was a tradition from Prophet Abraham (pbuh).

vocabulary.definition: The feeling of being thankful.
People who stay alive after a disaster.
Did not eat or drink for religious reasons.
A custom that people have kept for a long time.
To move out and cover a large area.

options: making a fire on the wooden ship
languageFocusExercises.explanation: A gerund (-ing form) can be the subject of a sentence: “Making a fire … was not allowed.”

feedback.correct: Correct. The gerund phrase is the subject.

languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose the correct form for each sentence.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which form fits?

formChoices.sentence: [choice] a fire on the wooden ship was not allowed.
They fasted on this day to thank Allah for [choice] them.
Nobody [choice] have a warm, cooked meal during the whole journey.

languageFocusExercises.title: Use: Showing Gratitude
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write five to six sentences about how your culture shows gratitude.
languageFocusExercises.question: What do people do? Why?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Example: “In my culture, people often cook a special meal after a difficult time. They share it with neighbors and the poor. Sharing food is a way of saying thank you. Some people also fast or give charity. Showing gratitude matters because it reminds us of the good things we have.”

pages.title: Ashura in Islam
pages.content: Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) also fasted on Ashura in Mecca and continued this after moving to Medina. He asked other Muslims to fast too. However, when the Qur’an required fasting during Ramadan, Ashura fasting became optional. After that, Muslims were free to fast on this day or not. Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) recommended fasting either on the 9th and 10th or on the 10th and 11th of Muharram.

vocabulary.definition: Said that something is good to do.

pages.title: Noah’s Last Advice
pages.content:
The Qur’an ends Noah’s story without details about what happened next. According to a hadith, Prophet Noah (pbuh) gave important advice to his sons, telling them to believe that there is no god but Allah, because this belief is more valuable than the whole universe. He also told them to stay away from giving partners to Allah and from being arrogant.

Noah’s last words summarize his lifelong struggle.

Give the main ideas in a short form.
Something that you think is true.
A long, hard effort to do something.

pages.title: Language Review
pages.content: Review and use the language of the whole book.

exercises.title: Notice: Where Does the Information Come From?
exercises.instructions: Sort the sentences by their source.
exercises.question: Which source does the book give?

items: Noah stayed with his people for 950 years.
The leaders said, “Verily, we see you in plain error.”
There were 80 believers on the Ark.

The Qur’an: Noah stayed with his people for 950 years.
The leaders said, “Verily, we see you in plain error.”
Reports and scholars: There were 80 believers on the Ark.

exercises.explanation: The book gives surah names for Qur’anic information, and words like “according to Islamic reports” or a scholar’s name for other information.

feedback.incorrect: Look for the surah names and “according to”.

exercises.title: Notice: The Passive
exercises.instructions: Choose the sentence with a correct passive form.
exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: The tablets were written in Sumer and Babylon.
The tablets were write in Sumer and Babylon.
The tablets written in Sumer and Babylon were.
exercises.explanation: The past passive is was / were + past participle: were written.

exercises.title: Notice: The Past Perfect
exercises.instructions: Is the sentence true or false?
exercises.question: In “Noah hurried to the ship he had built”, the building happened before he hurried.
exercises.explanation: The past perfect shows the earlier of two past actions.

exercises.title: Build: Linking Ideas
exercises.instructions: Choose the best linker for each sentence.
exercises.question: Which linker fits?

formChoices.sentence: [choice] Noah invited them to worship Allah alone, they insisted on their false belief.
Allah owns everything. [choice], there can only be one true Creator.
The poor believed his message. [choice], the rich leaders rejected it.

exercises.explanation: “Although” shows a contrast in one sentence, “therefore” a conclusion, and “yet” a contrast in a new sentence.

feedback.incorrect: Is it a contrast or a conclusion?

exercises.title: Build: Complete the Summary
exercises.instructions: Fill each gap from the word bank. Two words are not needed.
exercises.question: Which words complete the summary?
exercises.fillBlanksText: Noah is [blank] for his great determination. His people accused him of [blank]. The rich leaders refused to believe [blank] they wanted to keep their wealth. Noah told his sons to stay away from [blank] arrogant.
exercises.explanation: These patterns come from Chapters 1, 3, 5 and 11.

feedback.correct: Well done. Known, lying, as, being.

exercises.title: Build: Correct the Sentences
exercises.instructions: Find the mistake in each sentence and choose the correct form.
exercises.question: Which form is correct?

errorItems.sentence: They threatened stoning him to death.
Noah asked the believers board the ship.
This belief is more valuable as the whole universe.

exercises.explanation: Use “threaten to + verb”, “ask someone to + verb” and “more … than”.

feedback.correct: Correct. To stone, to board, than.
feedback.incorrect: Check the verb patterns and the comparative.

exercises.title: Build: Say It Another Way
exercises.instructions: Complete the new sentence. Keep the same meaning.
exercises.question: How else can we say it?

transformItems.source: This event is known as Noah’s Flood.
transformItems.frame: People [blank] this event Noah’s Flood.

transformItems.source: Making a fire on the wooden ship was not allowed.
transformItems.frame: They were not allowed to [blank] a fire on the wooden ship.

transformItems.source: His son did not accept the faith either.
transformItems.frame: [blank] his wife nor his son accepted the faith.

exercises.explanation: Passive to active, a gerund subject to “allowed to + verb”, and “either” to “neither … nor”.

exercises.title: Use: A New Context
exercises.instructions: Read about a school volunteer group. Fill each gap from the word bank.
exercises.question: Can you use the book’s words in a new text?
exercises.fillBlanksText: Our volunteer group helps families after floods. Our leader is a [blank] woman who never talks about herself. With great [blank], she organizes food and clothes every week. Many families who [blank] the last flood write to thank us. We feel deep [blank] for their kind letters.
exercises.explanation: Humble, determination, survived and gratitude come from the book. Here they describe a volunteer group today.

feedback.correct: Well done. You used the book’s words in a new text.
feedback.incorrect: Read the words around each gap.

exercises.title: Use: Check a Short Text
exercises.instructions: A student wrote about a storm. Find each mistake.
exercises.question: What should the student change?

errorItems.sentence: When we arrived home, the rain already had stopped.
My mother asked us stay inside.
Go out in a storm is dangerous.

exercises.explanation: Put “already” between had and the past participle. Use “ask someone to + verb”. A gerund can be a subject.

feedback.correct: Correct. Had already stopped, to stay, Going out.
feedback.incorrect: Check the past perfect, the verb pattern and the subject.

exercises.title: Use: A Lesson for Today
exercises.instructions: Write six to eight sentences about one lesson from Noah’s story for people today.
exercises.question: Which lesson is most important? Why?
exercises.explanation: Example: “One lesson from Noah’s story is equality. In Chapter 5, the rich leaders wanted Noah to send away his poor followers. Although they were powerful, Noah refused. He knew that the poor believers were sincere. Today, some people still look down on others because of money. Therefore, we should judge people by their character. We can do this by treating every classmate with the same respect.”

feedback.correct: Check: evidence from the book, although or therefore, and by + -ing.

discussionPrompts.question: Name the lesson and give evidence from the book.
discussionPrompts.example: One lesson from Noah’s story is … In Chapter …, …

discussionPrompts.question: Say how people can follow it today.
